To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the failure of RF cavities in SSR0 section of the Project-X linac can be compensated with the help of solenoid field and the failure of solenoid in same section can also be compensated by the RF field of the cavity.
the failure of RF Cavity and Solenoid in SSR1 results in beam emittance dilution which is compensated by changing the beam parameters in the following section.
the failure of RF cavities in SSR0 section can be compensated using the beam line elements like solenoid and quadrupole magnets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of beam dynamics and its compensation for the failure of beam line element at low energy.
the study of the beam dynamics in the case of the failure of RF and solenoid in CW superconducting Linac, and the compensation for these failures.
the following aspects: (i) The effect of failure of RF cavity and solenoid on the beam parameters and beam losses in the following sections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the failure of beamline element in CW linac is not a critical issue as long as the failure is detected before the beam reaches to the next section and the beam is re-matched accordingly.
the failure of RF cavities and solenoids in the SSR0 section would result in the mis-match of the SSR0 section and following sections of the Project-X linac.
, the effects of failure of RF cavity and solenoid in CW superconducting linacs are very critical and need to be compensated properly to avoid the beam losses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the beam dynamics studies for the failure of beamline elements are important to be performed before the commissioning of the machine, as the compensation of the beam parameters is possible by using different correction schemes, and it will be helpful in the operation of the Linac.
the failure of RF and solenoid elements at SSR0 section would lead to the emittance growth and beam losses.
, the effects of failure of beam line components can be compensated by the proper design of the beam line elements.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the failure of RF and solenoid elements at low energy can cause beam losses at high energies and the beam losses are dependent on the failure time of the element.
the compensation for the failed RF cavity & solensoid is not only possible but it can be done with minimum impact on the following section.
, the failure of the beam line element in SSR0 section can be compensated with the help of beam diagnostics and beam line elements.
